correctness.rationale: For p,q≥2,d=p+q-1,h∈[1,3], the graph shortest-path metric gives cross edges 1 except a_1b_1=h, with a three-hop alternative at h=3. The determinant-one change t=f(b_1),u_i=f(a_{i+1})−t,v_j=f(b_{j+1}) reduces the entire anchored ball to coordinate cubes and |t+u_i−v_j|≤1,|t|≤h. Differentiation at ±h is justified by Fubini/slab sections and sign symmetry. For h≥1 the upper inequalities lead to min v−max u≥h−1, and integration of the u maximum gives S(h)=(p−1)!(q−1)!/(d−1)!·(3−h)^{d−1}. Thus V′(h)=2S(h). The h=1 baseline follows from range density p(p−1)r^{p−2} and beta integral, V(1)=2^d p!q!/d!. Integrating proves the displayed V(h), its strict growth, h=3 redundant-edge ratio, derivative vanishing through order d−1 and nonzero dth derivative, with fixed-n pq comparison. Independently enumerated 12 rational/integer Ehrhart cases directly from original anchored inequalities and four symbolic derivative examples. Finite tests corroborate but do not replace the all-parameter analytic proof.

value.rationale: The object and invariant are intrinsically motivated: quantitative Lebesgue-volume response of a finite-metric Lipschitz dual unit ball as a single cross-edge constraint weakens and becomes redundant. The exact all-p,q and all-real-h law determines a sharp d-th order contact at edge deletion and a nontrivial relative gain 2/(pq), distinguishing balanced from unbalanced bicliques. This is not a routine substitution into the known undeformed volume or merely a tiny finite enumeration, and serves as a precise benchmark for metric/polytope perturbation geometry.
